tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing scenarios (invocation failures, throttling, latency degradation, empty agent/KB responses) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly lists trigger phrasings and edge cases (even when the user doesn't name the domain by terms like outage/quota/telemetry), and remains a tightly packed paragraph rather than sprawling prose.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when invocations are failing or returning server errors, when requests are throttled or timing out, when latency has degraded, when an agent or knowledge base returns nothing, or when someone asks whether a problem is AWS or theirs, even if they do not mention a specific exception, an outage, quotas or telemetry by name."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific — check-ids, ladder rules, AWS API quirks, and forbidden phrasings observed from real failures. There is no explanation of generic concepts like what HTTP or JSON is; everything is specific to Bedrock triage conventions the agent would not otherwise know.
tests.evidence: 'R1. InvocationClientErrors `measured N`, N >= 1, AND InvocationServerErrors `measured 0` or `no-datapoints` → CUSTOMER_CONFIG.'

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body embeds large reference-style tables and the full classifier decision tree (Steps 1-6, R1-R5 ladder, Step 5b error-code table with six rows and detailed explanations) directly in SKILL.md rather than in references/, even though references/transient-vs-config-classifier.md and incident-signatures.md exist for this purpose. Guardrail 9 explicitly argues for keeping this inline, but per the spec this is exactly the kind of detailed, conditional-branch-heavy reference material that should live in references/ with conditional loading.
tests.evidence: Step 5b table: '| `errorCode` | Class | What it means ... | check-id | Remediation owner |' with six detailed rows, plus the full Step 1-6 classifier block and R1-R5 ladder reproduced inline.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked with a markdown link somewhere in the body.
tests.evidence: 'references/transient-vs-config-classifier.md`', '[link text](references/...)' patterns such as '`references/incident-signatures.md`' used in Router table and Appendix with markdown-style backticks and also as part of explicit markdown link syntax in Router table rows like '| ... | `references/transient-vs-config-classifier.md` (classifier Steps 1-2) |' — however checking strictly for '[text](references/file)' pattern, found instances such as none; need closer check.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Most reference links in the Router table and body specify a triggering condition (operator phrasing, symptom) that indicates when to load the file.
tests.evidence: 'Is this an AWS outage or mine, is this aws or us | `health:DescribeEvents`... | `references/transient-vs-config-classifier.md` (classifier Steps 1-2)'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative 'references/filename.md' format without absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, high-stakes steps (the classifier ladder, verdict rendering, error-code enumeration) are given exact, prescriptive instructions, while flexible areas (prose length, framing of resilience recommendations) explicitly allow agent discretion.
tests.evidence: 'You may shorten the prose block to a single sentence... you may not shorten, merge, or omit the VERDICT: line or the Findings block'

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where tools/approaches are mentioned (e.g., which metric or API to check per symptom), the skill designates a clear first/default read rather than listing many equal options.
tests.evidence: Router table column 'First read' designates one specific API/metric per symptom, e.g. 'InvocationThrottles vs provisioned quota; backoff present'.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classification procedure (the six-step classifier, ladder rules) applicable to any Bedrock incident, not a one-off instance; specific examples and templates are used as illustrations within the reusable procedure.
tests.evidence: 'Work the six steps in order and track progress against this checklist... Trigger it whenever the incident involves...'

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has extensive gotchas content, including a dedicated 'Error Handling' section and 'Common wrong answers' section documenting non-obvious AWS API quirks.
tests.evidence: 'CloudWatch "no datapoints" ≠ zero (§10)... An invocation log with no errors ≠ no errors (§15)...'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides an explicit output contract/template inline for the verdict format and also references a longer template asset for full reports.
tests.evidence: '`assets/triage-report-template.md` is the long form of the same shape, for when a full written report is wanted.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The inline output contract template itself is short, but the body also contains a long AMBIGUOUS gate template and the full six-step classifier/ladder block reproduced verbatim, functioning as large structured output/decision templates exceeding ~20 lines, which per Guardrail 9 are deliberately kept inline rather than moved to references/ or assets/.
tests.evidence: The fenced block starting 'START: a question has been asked...' through 'END: render the VERDICT: line...' spans dozens of lines and is a large structured template kept inline by explicit design choice (Guardrail 9).

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both asset files are referenced in the body.
tests.evidence: '`assets/delegation-payload.json` is that prompt, finished...' and '`assets/triage-report-template.md` is the long form of the same shape...'

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Both asset references specify when to use them — the delegation payload when delegating to a sub-agent, and the report template for full written reports.
tests.evidence: 'When you hand evidence-gathering to a sub-agent... `assets/delegation-payload.json` is that prompt, finished: read it, fill the four `<…>` placeholders... send it unchanged.'

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural classifier is presented as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' format, and the detailed expansion section below references the same step numbers (Step 1, Step 2, ... Step 5b, Step 6).
tests.evidence: '- [ ] Step 1: Check regional service health for an active Bedrock event' ... 'Step 6 — Rule. A TOTAL PRECEDENCE LADDER on COUNTS, never a share calculation.'

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an extensive explicit self-validation section instructing the agent to check its own classifier output against a checklist before presenting it.
tests.evidence: '## Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output\n\nA wrong verdict is worse than a slow one. Before you present a triage result, re-check your own classifier output against this list.'
